receptacle.meaning: A container for keeping things in.

ordeal.meaning: A hard, painful experience that you must go through.

nettled.meaning: Slightly angry because of something that was said.

bandbox.meaning: A round box made of thin board, used to keep a woman's things for the head.

wheedler.meaning: A person who gets what he wants by saying sweet things he does not mean.

plummy.meaning: Very good and nice. Here Laurie uses it for an interesting piece of news.

jubilee.meaning: A time of great happiness and a party.

bedewed.meaning: Made wet with small drops. Here it means wet with water from the eyes.

billiard.meaning: A game played on a big table with balls and long sticks. In those days a billiard room was a place respectable girls thought bad.

paragraphs.context: If anyone had been watching her, he would have thought her movements decidedly peculiar
paragraphs.mainIdea: Jo goes to a newspaper office in town but is too nervous to go in. She walks up and down in the street, and Laurie watches her.
paragraphs.simple: If anyone had watched Jo, he would have thought her actions very strange. When she got off the bus, she walked very fast to a certain number in a certain busy street. She found the place with some trouble, went to the door and looked up the dirty stairs. After standing completely still for a minute, she suddenly ran back into the street and walked away as fast as she had come. She did this several times, and it greatly amused a black-eyed young man who was resting in a window of the building across the street. When she came back for the third time, Jo gave herself a shake, pulled her hat over her eyes and went up the stairs, looking as if she were going to have all her teeth pulled out.

sentences.context: Because if you care much about riches, you will never go and marry a poor man
sentences.simple: If you care a lot about money, you will never marry a poor man.
sentences.grammar: This is a real 'if' sentence (first conditional): 'if' + present tense, then 'will never' for the result.

up to mischief.example: You are up to some mischief, Jo

play fair.meaning: To act honestly and follow the rules.
play fair.example: Play fair, Teddy, or I'll never believe you
